title: FromExt
description:
A message from the extension process to the host. Its JSON Schema is
`schemas/extension-to-core.schema.json` (`docs/specs/protocols.md` §10).

oneOf.description: One of its timed actions is open for `closes_in_ms` more, or closed when that's absent.
The answer to `camera_picture`: the picture, or why there's none.
Every entity, and whether time and sun triggers can be armed. `registry:read`.
Every entity's current state. `states:read`.
The recent changes of these entities since `since`, oldest first. `history:read`.

What a person can see and may do now, for checking a flow of theirs. Only an extension
whose manifest says `users = true` is answered (`docs/specs/access.md` §4.1).

Something the engine did to the home, for the activity log. No answer. The core takes
only `flow_turned_off` and `flow_handed_over`, and only from an extension that limits
what people can do.
Start receiving `state_changed` and/or `registry_changed`. `events:read`.
Ask an entity to do something, as a run of this engine. `services:call`.

command.description: The action: `turn_on`, `set_value`, … or `toggle`, which the core resolves.

data.description: The action's data, as its service takes it (`docs/specs/protocols.md` §7.1).

oneOf.description: The answer to an `app_request` from the extension's page.

AlarmStatus.description: What a panel is doing. Home Assistant's `AlarmControlPanelState`.

oneOf.description: Something tripped it, and it's counting down before it sounds.
Told to arm, and counting down so people can leave.
Going off.

ArmMode.description: A way a panel is armed. Home Assistant's names.

oneOf.description: People are in: the doors and windows, not the rooms.
Nobody is in.
People are in and asleep.
Nobody is in for a while.
With some of its sensors left out.

AttributeKey.description: Format of a slug (attribute key): lowercase letters a-z and digits, in words separated by single `_`. 1-64 characters.

AvailabilityTarget.description: Which entities a change of availability applies to (spec §6.4).

oneOf.description: Every entity of this device.

BinarySensorClass.description:
What a binary sensor's `on` means: Home Assistant's binary sensor device classes, by the
same names.

ButtonClass.description: What pressing it does, when that's one of Home Assistant's.

oneOf.description: Makes the device show itself: a blink, a beep.
Installs an update the device has.

CameraStatus.description: What a camera is doing. Home Assistant's camera states, with `off` for one turned off.

oneOf.description: Someone is watching it live.

Capabilities.description: What an entity can do, per kind. Static facts that don't change with its state.

color_temp_kelvin.description: Supports color temperature, within this range.

options.description:
Every text it can report, when that's a fixed list (a washing machine's program, Home
Assistant's `enum` sensors). Only for text; readings outside it are refused, and rules
comparing it with text it can never have are refused when saved.

state_class.description: How numeric readings accumulate, for history and statistics.

value_type.description: Whether readings are numbers or text. Rules are type-checked against this.

device_class.description: What it measures, from the same list as a sensor's.

max.description: The highest value it takes. Not below `min`.

mode.description: How a page should offer it.

step.description: The smallest change that means anything, e.g. `0.5`. Above zero.

options.description: Every choice it has, at least one.

max_length.description: The most characters it takes, at most 255.

mode.description: Whether it's a secret, which pages don't show.

pattern.description:
A regular expression the text has to match, as the device says. The device checks it;
Irori shows it to whoever is typing.

event_types.description: Everything it can report happening, at least one, e.g. `single`, `double`, `long`.

position.description: Can be sent to a position between open and closed, and says where it is.

stop.description: Can be stopped while it's moving.

tilt.description: Has slats that tilt, and says how far.

code_format.description:
A regular expression the code matches, as the device says. The device checks it; pages
show it to whoever is typing.

open.description: Can open the door as well as unlock it, e.g. by pulling the latch.

requires_code.description: Needs a code to lock, unlock or open.

oscillate.description: Can swing from side to side.

speed_count.description:
How many speeds it has, 0 when its speed can't be set. Speeds are set and reported as a
percentage; this says how many steps there really are.

position.description: Can be opened part of the way, and says how far.

stop.description: Can be stopped while it moves.

duration.description: Can be told for how long.

tones.description: The tones it can sound. Empty when there's no choice.

hvac_modes.description: The modes it can be put in, at least one.

max_temp.description: The highest target it takes, in °C.

min_temp.description: The lowest target it takes, in °C.

target_humidity.description: Takes a target humidity, within this range in %.

target_temperature_range.description: Takes a range: heat below the low end, cool above the high one.

temp_step.description: How finely a target can be set, in °C, e.g. 0.5.

max_temp.description: The highest target it takes, in °C.

min_temp.description: The lowest target it takes, in °C.

on_off.description:
Has its own on and off, apart from its modes. While it's off its mode reads `off`, even
when `off` isn't one of its `operation_modes`.

operation_modes.description: The modes it can be put in, at least one.

temp_step.description: How finely a target can be set, in °C.

humidity.description: The target humidities it takes, in %.

play_media.description: Can be told to play a piece of media.

queue.description: Has a queue to skip through.

seek.description: Playback can jump to a position.

check.description: Can be told to look for a newer version now.

install.description: Can be told to install. Without it, it only says an update exists.

arm_modes.description: The ways it can be armed. A panel with none can only be disarmed and watched.

code_arm_required.description: Needs its code to arm. Only means something with a `code_format`.

code_disarm_required.description: Needs its code to disarm. Only means something with a `code_format`.

code_format.description:
What its code looks like, when it takes one: digits, or any text. Pages show a keypad
for the first.

trigger.description: Can be set off on purpose.

oneOf.description: What a `date`, a `time` or a `datetime` can do: hold its value. Nothing to say yet.
What a `date`, a `time` or a `datetime` can do: hold its value. Nothing to say yet.
What a `date`, a `time` or a `datetime` can do: hold its value. Nothing to say yet.

clean_spot.description: Can clean the spot it's on.

fan_speeds.description: The fan speeds it has, by its own names (`quiet`, `turbo`). None for one with no choice.

locate.description: Can make a noise so someone can find it.

pause.description: Can be paused where it is.

return_home.description: Can be sent back to its dock.

start.description: Can be told to start cleaning.

dock.description: Can be sent back to its dock.

pause.description: Can be paused where it is.

start_mowing.description: Can be told to start mowing.

oneOf.description: What a scene can do: be set. Nothing to say yet.

source_type.description: How it knows, when it says. Home Assistant's source types.

oneOf.description: What a timer can do. Nothing to say yet: every timer starts, pauses, and ends.
What a schedule can do. Nothing to say yet: a schedule is read, not told.

motion_detection.description: Watches for motion, and can be told to stop and start again.

on_off.description: Can be turned off and on again: a privacy switch.

ColorTempRange.description: Supported color temperatures in kelvin, `min` (warmest) to `max` (coolest).

ContextId.description: A ULID: 26 characters, uppercase Crockford base32.

CoverClass.description: What it covers, when that's one of Home Assistant's.

DeviceDescription.description:
A device as a protocol describes it. The core adds it to the registry, or updates the
entry with the same `unique_id`.

serial_number.description: The serial number the device reports for itself.

suggested_area.description:
An area name the device reports for itself, e.g. ESPHome's `area`. The core uses it only
when the device is new and the user hasn't assigned an area.

unique_id.description: The protocol's permanent handle for the device, e.g. its MAC address.

via_device_unique_id.description: The `unique_id` of the bridge or hub this device is reached through.

EntityCategory.description:
What an entity is to its device, when it isn't what the device is for: a light's power-on
behaviour is a setting, its signal strength a diagnostic. Home Assistant's names.
Ordered as pages list them: settings before diagnostics, and both after an entity with none.

oneOf.description: Changes how the device behaves, e.g. a motion sensor's timeout.
Tells how the device is doing, e.g. its signal strength or firmware version.

EntityDescription.description:
An entity as a protocol describes it. The core adds it to the registry, or updates the
entry with the same `unique_id`.

capabilities.description: What it can do. `capabilities.kind` is the entity's kind.

device_unique_id.description: The `unique_id` of the device it belongs to. The device must be described first.

entity_category.description: Whether it's one of the device's settings or diagnostics rather than something it's for.

name.description:
Leave out for a device's main feature (e.g. the relay of a smart plug): the entity then
uses its device's name, and must have `device_unique_id`.

suggested_object_id.description:
What to call it after the `.` in its entity id, when it's new. Otherwise the core derives
one from the names.

unique_id.description: The protocol's permanent handle for the entity.

EntityId.description: An entity id: `<kind>.<object_id>`, e.g. `light.hallway`. The object id uses lowercase letters a-z and digits in words separated by single `_`, 1-64 characters.

EventClass.description: What kind of thing it reports happening, when that's one of Home Assistant's.

oneOf.description: A button being pressed: a remote's, a wall switch's.

Health.description: What the protocol says about itself (spec §6.5).

oneOf.description: Working, with a problem worth showing, e.g. "2 of 5 devices unreachable".

HvacAction.description:
What it's doing right now, which can differ from its mode: set to heat, but idle because
the room is warm enough.

HvacMode.description: What it's set to do: Home Assistant's modes.

oneOf.description: Heats or cools to stay within a range.
Follows its own schedule or logic.

LinkQuality.description:
A link's quality, in the four steps a person reads it in. Raw numbers (an RSSI, an LQI)
change from one report to the next; these don't, unless the link really does.

oneOf.description: Stuck: it tried and couldn't finish.

MediaPlayerClass.description: What kind of player it is.

MowerActivity.description: What a mower is doing. Home Assistant's `LawnMowerActivity`.

oneOf.description: On its way back to the dock.
Stuck, or something is wrong with it.

Name.description: A human-readable name. 1-100 characters, no leading or trailing whitespace.

Network.description: One network a protocol reaches its devices over.

detail.description: A few words about it: "Channel 15, PAN 0x1a62".

name.description: What it's called on the map: "Zigbee", "Matter". Without one, the extension's name.

scanned_at.description:
When its links were last measured, for a network whose links are measured when asked
(Zigbee's scan) rather than all the time.

NetworkLink.description: Two nodes that reach each other directly.

from.description: The node further from the controller, when that's known.

quality.description: How good the link is, when the protocol can tell.

reading.description:
The measurement behind the quality, short enough to draw on the link: `LQI 212`,
`-54 dBm`, `USB`.

NetworkMedium.description: How a node is connected, or what a link is over.

oneOf.description: A cable into the machine: a USB dongle, a serial port.
The home's network, not known which way.
The internet: between Irori and a vendor's cloud, or a vendor's cloud and a device.

NetworkNode.description:
Something on the network: Irori itself, a coordinator, a border router, an access point, a
device.

detail.description: A few words more: "Router, channel 25", "Google Nest Hub".

device_unique_id.description: The device it is, when it's one of the protocol's devices in Irori.

host.description:
Its host name on the home's network, as mDNS gives it (`fuchsia-dce5-5ba4-40db.local`),
when the protocol knows. Two protocols that see the same box (a Nest Hub is a Cast device
and a Thread border router) name it the same, and the map draws it once. [`host_name`]
makes it.

id.description: Its id in this map, which links name: 1-64 of letters, digits and `_.:-`.

medium.description: How it's connected, when the protocol knows.

NetworkRole.description: What a node does on the network.

oneOf.description:
Irori, or the controller it runs (the Matter server). Every network's is drawn as the one
Irori.
The radio a mesh is run from, on Irori's side: a Zigbee coordinator, a bridge.
Joins a mesh to the home's network: a Thread border router.
A Wi-Fi access point.
Passes a mesh's messages on: a Thread or Zigbee router.
On a mesh, through a router, and always listening.
On a mesh, through a router, and asleep most of the time: a battery sensor.
On the home's own network, Wi-Fi or wired.

A vendor's servers on the internet, which a cloud protocol reaches its devices through:
SwitchBot's, Tesla's. Drawn as the way into that protocol's devices.

NumberMode.description: How a page offers a number: a slider, a box to type in, or whichever suits the range.

ObjectId.description: Format of a slug (object id): lowercase letters a-z and digits, in words separated by single `_`. 1-64 characters.

OpenState.description: Where something that opens and closes is: a cover's or a valve's.

Playback.description: What it's doing. The primary value automations compare.

oneOf.description: Switched off, or the TV isn't showing this source.
On, with nothing playing. A backdrop counts as this.
The TV is in standby. Only when the device says so.

SecretRequest.description:
Where a secret goes: a path inside the extension's table in `secrets.toml`
(`docs/specs/config.md`). The extension decides the path, so the UI and the core can take a
secret for any extension without knowing what it means.

hint.description: Where to find it, e.g. "`api: encryption: key:` in the device's YAML".

label.description: What to call the field, e.g. "Encryption key".

path.description:
Table keys from the extension's own table down to the value, e.g.
`["keys", "00:11:22:33:44:55"]`. At least one, and none empty — the same rules
[`crate::ExtensionSettings::set`] enforces when the secret is written.

SensorClass.description:
What a sensor measures: Home Assistant's sensor device classes, by the same names. A
sensor whose readings come from a fixed list says so with `options` instead of a class.

oneOf.description: Carbon dioxide; Home Assistant's `carbon_dioxide`.

SensorValue.description: A sensor reading: a finite number or text, matching the sensor's `value_type`.

State.description: A typed value, tagged with the entity kind it belongs to.

brightness.description: 1-255, when the light supports dimming. Kept while off: the level it returns to.

color_mode.description: Which color setting is active, when the light supports more than one.

on.description: `true` means detected/open/wet/etc., depending on the device class.

option.description: The choice it's on: one of its options.

event_type.description: What happened last: one of its `event_types`.

tilt.description: 0 (closed) to 100 (open), for one whose slats tilt.

percentage.description: Its speed, 1-100, when it has speeds. Kept while off: the speed it comes back on at.

preset_mode.description: One of its `preset_modes`, when it's in one.

current_temperature.description: The room's temperature, as it measures it, in °C.

target_temp_low.description: In °C, for one that takes a range.

target_temperature.description: In °C, for one that takes a single target.

current_humidity.description: The room's humidity, as it measures it, in %.

app.description: The app that's showing, when it says.

duration.description: How long the current media is, in seconds.

position.description: Where playback is, in seconds, when it can seek.

state.description: What it's doing. Its typed value, for rules (`text()`).

available.description: A newer version than the installed one is there to install, and it isn't the skipped one.

last_error.description:
Why the last install didn't finish: the protocol's reason when it has one, otherwise the
core's. The next install clears it.

progress.description: How far the install has got, in %, from a device that says.

release_summary.description: A few words on what the latest version changes.

release_url.description: Where the full release notes are.

skipped_version.description: The version someone chose to pass over. The core sets it; a protocol's is ignored.

title.description: What the software is called, when that isn't the device's name.

fan_speed.description: One of its `fan_speeds` (checked by the core).

accuracy.description: How far off the position may be, in metres.

duration.description: How long it runs when started without being told, in seconds.

finishes_at.description: When it runs out. While it's active, and only then.

remaining.description: Seconds left. While it's paused, and only then.

next_change.description: When it next turns on or off. Absent for a schedule that never changes (an empty week).

on.description: Within one of its times now.

motion_detection.description: Whether it's watching for motion, for one with `motion_detection`.

oneOf.description: A current value, e.g. temperature.
A running total that can go up or down, e.g. net energy.
A counter that only increases, resetting occasionally, e.g. a meter reading.

StateReport.description:
A new value for one entity, from its protocol. The core adds the timestamps and context,
and checks the value against the entity's kind and capabilities.

Reporting a value doesn't change the entity's availability; that's reported separately.

attributes.description: Replaces all of the entity's attributes. Leave out to clear them.

caused_by.description:
The context of the service call that caused this change, when the protocol knows it
(e.g. the device confirmed a command). Otherwise the change is attributed to the device.

replayed.description:
The protocol is repeating what it last heard rather than hearing something new, e.g. a
retained MQTT message delivered on (re)subscribing. For an `event`, whose every report is
an occurrence, a replayed one sets the value without counting as something happening.

state.description:
The typed value, or `null` if the device doesn't know it (e.g. it just restarted). Must be
present even when `null`.

oneOf.description: Not counting: never started, run out, or cancelled.
Counting down.
Stopped part of the way, with time left.

Timestamp.description: RFC 3339 timestamp with an offset, e.g. 2026-09-15T22:04:31.120Z. Uppercase T and Z, seconds 00-59 (no leap seconds), at most 9 fractional digits, offset -23:59 to +23:59. Serialized in UTC.

oneOf.description: A position from satellites, or from a phone that says where it is.
Seen on the home's network.

UniqueId.description: Stable id assigned by the protocol (e.g. a Zigbee IEEE address). Unique within the protocol.

Unmodeled.description:
Something a protocol found that Irori has no entity kind for yet: a device's fan, its
infrared blaster. See `docs/specs/protocols.md` §6.7.

Not an entity: it has no id, no state, and nothing can be asked of it. It's listed on its
device (or its extension, without one) so a person can see what's there and isn't supported,
rather than a device that looks like it has less than it does. When Irori gains the kind, the
protocol describes it as an entity instead, and it drops off this list.

device_unique_id.description: The device it's on, when it's on one.

name.description: Its name, when the protocol knows one.

platform.description:
What the protocol calls this kind of thing, e.g. `fan`, `infrared`. Deliberately not an
entity kind: it's one Irori doesn't have.

reason.description:
Why Irori can't use it, when it's a kind Irori has but this one couldn't be read: its
command needs a template Irori doesn't run, say. Absent for a kind Irori doesn't have.

oneOf.description: A device's firmware.

UserId.description: Format of a slug (user id): lowercase letters a-z and digits, in words separated by single `_`. 1-64 characters.

VacuumActivity.description: What a vacuum is doing. Home Assistant's `VacuumActivity`.

oneOf.description: Off its dock and doing nothing.
On its way back to the dock.
Stuck, or something is wrong with it.

Waiting.description:
Something a protocol found but can't use yet, because it needs a person first: a device
that wants an encryption key, one that has to be paired, an account that has to be signed in
to. See `docs/specs/protocols.md` §6.6.

Not a device in the registry. It has no entities and nothing is known about it beyond what
it announced, so putting it there would show a device that can't do anything. It's listed on
its extension instead, where the UI can offer to fix it.

name.description: What it calls itself, for recognising it.

reason.description: What's needed, in a sentence, e.g. "it wants an encryption key".

secret.description: Where a secret that would unlock it goes, if a secret is what it needs.

unique_id.description:
The same handle the device will have once it's in the registry, so what a person
provides now is attached to what it's for (ROADMAP D31).

WirePicture.description: A picture on the wire: its type, and its bytes as base64.

WireServiceError.description: A failed service call on the wire (`docs/specs/protocols.md` §7.3).
